name: Whalefolk
body:
Possibly the largest humanoids other than giants, these immense creatures are reminiscent of the largest toothed whales.

Appearance

Whalefolk tower above other humanoids, standing nearly 20 feet tall with a wide tail that extends another 10 feet behind them.

Their bodies are wide and firm, while their heads are long and square like those of sperm whales, with small eyes and toothy recessed jaws. They do not have noses, instead having blow holes on the back of their heads. Their skin is thick and rubbery, and usually gray in color-but can also be white, black, blue, or green.

Social

Whalefolk are communal creatures. They form small, semi-aquatic communities centered strongly around family ties. They are optimistic and outgoing-but also very protective and not afraid to defend themselves against threats.

Whalefolk are not as populous as many of the landbound and aquatic species that surround them. They reproduce slowly, and each new child is met with great celebration.

Whalefolk mature slowly, finally reach full size and adulthood around 40 years of age.

At that time, many of them make their first journey away from the safety of their home pod-often traveling to explore the world, visit other far-flung whalefolk communities, and learn more about other aquatic and surface cultures.

Alignment and Religion

There is a strong sense of community and tradition ingrained in every whalefolk child from birth, leading to most being Lawful in alignment. Most are either Neutral or Good, with few outright Evil in intent.

Whalefolk do not have consistent religious practices from community to community.

Many worship nature spirits, led by a shaman or druid, but some communities venerate a single deity, usually a champion of nature, oceans, or family.

Names

Some typical whalefolk names include the following (choose or roll 1d12): 1 Burri, 2 Daufoi, 3 Hyloor, 4 Koda, 5 Kohola, 6 Koopira, 7 Muriyaa, 8 Oohaioha, 9 Ruby, 10 Tafooya, 11 Tellryoo, 12 Yalinwa

Common Traits
Ability Score Modifiers You are resilient and personable, but somewhat naïve and not overly strong for your size. Your ability score modifiers are +2 Con, +2 Cha, -2 Str, -4 Wis [mixed weakness]. (-2) After your modifiers for being size Huge are incorporated, your net ability score modifiers are: +2 Str, +2 Con, +2 Cha, -4 Dex, -4 Wis.
Size As a Huge creature, you have a -2 size penalty on attack rolls, a -2 size penalty to your Armor Class, a +2 size bonus to your CMB, and a -8 size penalty on Stealth checks. As a Huge creature, you occupy a space of 15 feet by 15 feet. Your reach is 10 feet. You take a further -4 penalty to Dex, and gain a further +4 bonus to Str. (14)
Type You are a Humanoid with the whalefolk subtype. (0)
Speed Your base speed is 20 feet. Your speed is never modified by armor or encumbrance. (-1)
Languages You begin play speaking Common. If you have a high Intelligence score, you can choose from any language of the following languages: Aquan, Elven, Giant, or Sylvan. (0)
Other Traits
Blubber Your thick, rubbery skin provides you with cold resistance 5 and a +2 natural armor bonus to AC. (4)
Echolocation In the water, you can emit a series of clicks, then instinctively pinpoint nearby creatures by hearing the echo. This ability gives you blindsense 30 feet against creatures that are touching the same body of water. A silence spell or similar effect negates your echolocation ability. (1)
Hold Breath Your enormous lungs allow you go without air much longer than most creatures. You can hold your breath 10 times as long as a normal creature (20 rounds for every point of your Constitution score). (1)
Reach Your reach is 10 feet. (1)
Slapping Tail You have a tail you can use to make attacks of opportunity with a reach of 10 feet. The tail is a natural attack that deals 2d6 points of damage plus 1-1/2 times your Strength modifier. (3)
Swim You have a swim speed of 30 feet and gain the +8 species bonus on Swim checks that a swim speed normally grants. (2)
Undersized Grip Despite being of Huge size, you have short, stubby arms and hands. You must use weapons sized for Large creatures. Likewise, you deal damage with unarmed attacks as if you were a Large creature instead of a Huge one. (-2)
Total: 21 RP (monstrous)
Variant Orcafolk

An offshoot of the more common whalefolk, this subspecies look like killer whales. They are more perceptive than common whalefolk, but are more primal and aggressive-placing more importance on instinct and less on formal teaching.

Ability Score Modifiers. Your ability score modifiers (including the adjustments for being Large) are +2 Str, +2 Con, +2 Cha, -2 Dex, -2 Int. This trait alters your size and ability score modifiers.
Size. Large.
Bite You gain a bite attack. This is a primary natural attack that deals 1d6 damage. This trait replaces undersized grip.
Alternate Traits
Big Brain Instead of being socially-focused like most whalefolk, you put your-quite literally-big brain to work uncovering knowledge. You gain a +2 bonus to Intelligence instead of Charisma. This trait alters ability score modifiers.
Deepsight You are specially adapted to the lightless depths of the oceans, but not to air-filled environments. You can see in the dark up to 120 feet while underwater, but do not gain this benefit out of water. This trait replaces echolocation.
Feybound The power of the Fey Realms courses through you. You gain low-light vision, DR 5/cold iron, and a +2 natural armor bonus to AC. This trait replaces blubber, echolocation, and hold breath.
Hatred You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls against aboleths and sahuagin. This trait replaces echolocation.
Landbound While most whalefolk are still tied to the sea, your pod migrated away from the coast and became firmly entrenched as landlubbers. Your land speed is 30 feet; your speed is still never modified by armor or encumbrance. You gain a +4 species bonus on Swim checks and can always take 10 while swimming. This trait alters speed, and replaces echolocation and swim.
Powerful Swimmer You use your tail not to attack but to propel you more swiftly through the water. Your swim speed increases to 50 feet. This trait replaces slapping tail.
Sailor Your love of the sea has made you a capable seafarer. You gain a +2 species bonus to Profession (sailor) checks. This trait replaces echolocation.
Weapon Familiarity You are proficient with nets, spears, and tridents. You treat harpoons as martial weapons rather than exotic ones. This trait replaces slapping tail.
Favored Class Bonuses
Bard Add +1 to your total number of bardic performance rounds per day.
Bloodrager Add +1 foot to your swim speed while bloodraging. This option has no effect unless you have selected it five times (or another increment of five).
Druid Add +1/2 to your wild empathy bonus when interacting with creatures that have the aquatic subtype.
Fighter Add +1 to your CMD when resisting a bull rush or reposition attempt.
Kineticist Add +1/5 of the Extra Wild Talent feat. This feat must be spent on a water-element talent.
Oracle Add +1/2 to your druid caster level when determining the range of any spells with the water descriptor.
Paladin Add +1 foot to the size of all your aura class features. This option has no effect unless you have selected it 5 times (or another increment of 5).
Rogue Add a +1/2 bonus on Perception checks while under or above the water.
Skald Add +1 to your total number of raging song rounds per day.
Sorcerer Add +1/2 point of cold damage to sorcerer spells you cast that deal cold damage.
Spirit Warrior Add +1/5 to your aura bonus when using the durability aura or presence aura.

Awesome Ancestries: Fantasy Animal Humanoids, Vol. 3 - Born to Be Wild. © 2025, Far Distant Future Publishing; Author: Bryan Mangum.
